constraints.title: Constraints
constraints.subtitle: Configure time and space constraints for schedule generation
constraints.maxDaysPerWeek: Max days per week per teacher
constraints.maxGapsPerDay: Max gaps per day per teacher
constraints.maxGapsPerWeek: Max gaps per week per teacher
constraints.courseMaxGapsPerDay: Max gaps per day per course
constraints.weightExplanation: Use the slider to set the weight from 0% to 100%. 100% means a strict constraint (required), lower values indicate the preference level for the engine to try to fulfill it. 0% disables the constraint.
constraints.maxHoursDailyDesc: Limits the maximum number of hours a teacher can teach in a single day. Example: Value = 6. A teacher will have at most 6 teaching blocks on any day.
constraints.maxConsecutiveDesc: Limits the number of consecutive hours a teacher can teach without a break. Example: Value = 4. The teacher will teach at most 4 hours in a row, then the engine will force a break.
constraints.maxDaysPerWeekDesc: The maximum number of days per week a teacher can have classes. Example: Value = 4. In a 5-day week, the teacher will have at least 1 day off.
constraints.maxGapsPerDayDesc: Limits the maximum number of 'gaps' (free blocks between classes) per day for a teacher. Example: Value = 0. The teacher will have a continuous schedule without intermediate gaps.
constraints.maxGapsPerWeekDesc: Limits the total number of 'gaps' allowed across the entire week for a teacher. Example: Value = 2. Throughout the week, the teacher will have at most 2 gaps.
constraints.minHoursDailyDesc: Ensures that if a teacher attends on a day, they have at least this minimum number of hours. Example: Value = 2. Prevents a teacher from coming in for just 1 hour.
constraints.courseMaxHoursDailyDesc: Limits the daily class hours for students of a course. Example: Value = 7. Students will not have more than 7 hours a day.
constraints.courseMaxGapsPerDayDesc: Limits the daily gaps allowed for students. Generally should be 0 to avoid students having free intermediate hours. Example: Value = 0.
constraints.minDaysBetweenActivitiesDesc: For subjects taught on multiple days, ensures separation. Example: Value = 1. Mathematics is taught on Monday and then at least on Tuesday (1 day difference).
constraints.consecutiveIfSameDayDesc: If a subject has multiple blocks on the same day, ensures they are scheduled consecutively. Example: Value = 1 (Yes). Language will have 2 consecutive hours.

faq.title: Everything you need to know
faq.subtitle: Clear answers to common questions about our automated school timetable software.
faq.q1: How does SyncroTime guarantee zero teacher or room conflicts?
faq.a1: SyncroTime incorporates an advanced combinatorial optimization engine. It rigorously validates millions of constraint permutations and will never assign a teacher or classroom to two overlapping activities.
faq.q2: Can I configure special constraints for part-time educators?
faq.a2: Yes. You have full granular control over individual availability, unavailable time slots, maximum consecutive teaching periods, and mandatory lunch or preparation breaks.
faq.q3: How does the 7-day free trial work?
faq.a3: When you sign up, you unlock immediate, unrestricted access to every feature for 7 days. You can input your actual school data, generate real timetables, and download PDF/Excel files with no upfront payment.
faq.q4: Can I export and print schedules for faculty and students?
faq.a4: Yes. SyncroTime generates publication-grade PDF documents formatted for printing (by grade, by teacher, and institution-wide master grids) along with fully editable Excel (.xlsx) spreadsheets.
faq.q5: What types of educational institutions can use SyncroTime?
faq.a5: SyncroTime supports primary and secondary schools, high schools, technical colleges, universities, and tutoring centers with custom daily and weekly structures.
